column2: Self-starting: the normal piston is quasi-powered by the redstone block (it touches the cell above the piston), fires at tick 1 and pushes observer B one cell so that it faces observer D. B lands (a moved observer fires 2 gt after it lands) while D sees the landing, so both are triggered in the same tick; that fixes the order of their ticks in every later handover as "the one turning off runs first": the pair runs in ANTI-PHASE, each on 2 gt exactly as the other turns off, P = 4 (a pair started by placing one observer always runs at P = 6). Steady-state family: observer only.

Three observers and two normal pistons (the redstone block is shoved aside in the warmup and stays). Steady state: a 10 gt loop (observer A; observer O2 watches A and fires on A's FALLING edge, 4 gt; O2 powers piston P2, whose head enters the cell O3 watches, 2 gt; O3 powers piston P1, which A watches: A fires 2 gt after P1 starts retracting, 2+2 gt) carrying TWO pulses 5 gt apart, so every component fires every 5 gt. The odd offset between the two pulses is made in the warmup (a piston fired by a block that lands in the block-entity phase acts a tick later).

A moving observer: the sticky piston (facing up) lifts the observer; it lands 2 gt later and its landing update makes the piston retract the next tick (landings happen in the block-entity phase: +1 gt); the observer is back down 2 gt later and fires 2 gt after landing (a moved observer always fires when it lands); its pulse strongly powers the note block behind it, which quasi-powers the piston: up again. 2 + 1 + 2 + 2 = 7 gt. The redstone block is pushed up out of the way in the warmup.

Observer C quasi-powers sticky piston A (C touches the cell above A, facing away from it); A shoves its payload (here a second sticky piston, never powered: any pushable block works) into the cell observer D watches, and C watches D. Each 2 gt pulse alternately pushes the payload (spit: it stays) and pulls it back (a pull-type pulse piston), and D fires on both moves: 2 pulses per 10 gt.

Two normal pistons facing up and two observers: B watches piston A1 and powers piston A2 behind it; C watches A2's head cell and quasi-powers A1 (C touches the cell above A1, facing away). Each piston move fires the other side's observer; retracting bases land in the block-entity phase, so the next move comes a tick later: an odd period, 3 pulses per 13 gt.

A loop of nine observers and one copper bulb (10 cells, a vertical 1x3x4 loop where some observers also touch non-consecutive loop members): the bulb's second edge and the shortcuts keep 12 pulses circulating unevenly; the observers repeat every 58 gt and the bulb's lit state (toggled on every rising edge) every 116 gt.
The same 10-cell loop as p116 with an iron trapdoor relay (opens and closes with its power, no toggle): 12 pulses circulating unevenly, P = 58.

Five observers and a note block around a 3x2 loop: the observer before the note block powers it, the next one watches it; the note block follows its power at once but takes a lattice cell, so the loop of 5 observers gives P = 10 (a loop of observers alone has an even count: P = 0 mod 4).

Divider chain on the observer pair: each copper bulb toggles on its power's rising edges (lit period doubles) and the comparator reading it powers the next bulb only every other pulse: 3 bulbs, P = 6 x 2^3 = 48 (`mctas clock obs divider --bulbs K`: P = P0 x 2^K, 3 blocks per stage).

The odd piston stage in a ring: observer O1 quasi-powers sticky piston S and O2 (watching O1) keeps S powered 4 gt from above, so the redstone block S pushes LANDS (block-entity phase) under normal piston Q, which fires the next tick: Q's head is seen by J 5 gt after O1 fired; J -> K1 -> K2 -> O1 closes the ring (2 gt each): P = 11, one pulse, 8 blocks flat.

Variant B of the odd piston stage: S pushes a slime block that drags the redstone block one cell further, which shifts Q and J by one cell so the ring back to O1 has an odd number of observers: P = 13. Taller towers give every odd period (oddring-p

in every/).
A first, longer layout of the odd piston stage (Q facing south): J -> 8 observers -> O1, P = 5 + 2 x 9 = 23.
